messages.text:
"Please make a game with the Stardew Valley vibe set in a fantasy world. For animal husbandry, use fantasy or mythical creatures; for farming, allow catching magical fish with magical plants and Marxies; and make the town a medieval fantasy village. Create a format similar to an open world, and in addition, add a mine, NPCs, NPC friendship levels, special friendship animations, and a first ending. Furthermore, include all the Stardew Valley systems. Do not make it exactly the same. It is a pixel art game. It features indie game sound. Create pixel art images for every item and improve the overall graphical quality. Also, remove emoticons and use pixel art instead.

When the game starts, there should be a loading screen with options to load a save file or start a new game. Loading allows you to replay a previously played game (allowing for multiple save points), while starting a new game allows you to create a character, choose your favorites, nickname, farm, and customize your character. Also, initially, you only have a hoe, 20 seeds, and a watering can; make it so you can purchase the rest of the tools and materials by collecting money from a shop.
Please let me go inside buildings to buy items.

Also, make the NPCs look different and change the buildings so they are distinguishable from the outside. Separate my house from the village. Make the screen change when I enter an alley from my house, and when I go from the alley to the village. Also, add crafting and recipes so I can make decorative items, various tools, useful items, and useful tools like chests, and add a huge variety of them.

Add a lot of plants, fish, monsters, and animals. Also, make the plants sold in shops different depending on the season, and make the items caught through fishing different depending on the season. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
